what: Integrated Visual Sprint 1 §八 -- Phase B typography closure: the Target's live DOM re-read and the local candidate proven against it with ONE reader, loaded-face proof included. Verdict first: every text-carrying style is live-equal and the loaded faces shape identical glyph bounds -- NO code change was needed, so Before == After for typography and zero product files were touched.
instrument: scripts/v5/t1-target-typography.mjs -- the sealed dual-side reader, extended this round with a fontProof block (document.fonts.check + two-fallback shaping detector + actualBoundingBox glyph bounds). Same code reads both sides; the collector was also fixed to pick a VISIBLE card (culled labels are display:none and render-aware innerText reads empty on them).

loadedFaceProof.claimStandard: no 'the code says Geist' -- proof is document.fonts status, fonts.check(), the two-fallback shaping test, and measured glyph bounds.
loadedFaceProof.target: family 'Geist' / 'Geist Mono' (variable, weight range 100-900), status loaded, check true, shapes true.
loadedFaceProof.local: family 'Geist Variable' / 'Geist Mono Variable' (@fontsource-variable 5.3.0), status loaded, check true, shapes true. No system-ui fallback anywhere.

glyphBoundsIdentity.note: ascent/descent/left/right of the probe string, px. Bit-equal at matched size and weight: the two names are the SAME variable font.

styleMatrix.textCarriers: meta, title, deck: fontWeight, fontSizePx, lineHeightPx, letterSpacingPx, textTransform, maxWidth, padding, opacity, overflow and lineCount ALL MATCH at all four viewports (title: 600 / 12cqw / leading 0.82 / tracking -0.085em / max-w 92%; deck: 500 / 2.5cqw / leading-tight / tracking -0.01em / max-w 58cqw / white 82%; meta: Mono 500 / 1.7cqw / tracking 0.18em / uppercase).
styleMatrix.containers: card box = plane box on both sides (sealed container law re-verified, object scale 1); se-clip overflow hidden matches the Target's clip; content padding 7cqw matches.

textPlaneDepth.note: [target tz, local tz] -- exact at every viewport.

residualDiffRows: container lineHeight 24px (inherited Tailwind root) vs 'normal' on OUR se-clip/se-content/se-rule -- these boxes carry no direct inline text, so the inherited value has no rendered effect; every text element sets its own matching line-height.
deck color serialization: Tailwind emits oklab(0.999994 ... / 0.82), ours rgba(255,255,255,0.82) -- the same white at 82% alpha.
lineCount on container rows: instrument artifact (the Target containers' first child is not a text node so the reader returns null there; text elements compare properly and match).

acceptance.labelsShownAllSides: every §四 still and recording carries labels + footer on both runtimes.
acceptance.titleNeverCrossesCards: se-clip overflow hidden (matched) + title localBox inside the card box + matching lineCounts.
acceptance.visualWeight: weight 600 with bit-equal glyph bounds -- same ink.
acceptance.lineBreaks: title and deck lineCounts match per viewport (content strings differ by design; the wrap LAW -- max-widths, leading, tracking -- is equal).
acceptance.metaDeckRule: matched (styleMatrix); the rule sits above the title on both sides.
acceptance.motionCoupling: labels ride the cards in all six real-input recordings (artifacts/integrated-review/*/recordings/) -- the CSS3D layer consumes the same layout frame as the renderer; no separation visible in slow drag, flick, wrap or orientation change.
acceptance.contentDifferences: by design: our catalog titles and the ATELIER footer brand (Iowan Old Style 700) replace the Target's titles and SHADER brand -- product content, not typography-system divergence.

codeChanges: NONE to product files. The §八 allowed files (TileLabelLayer, typography CSS, font loading, footer typography) were not touched: the re-proof passed everything. Only the reader script gained its fontProof block.
priorStatus: Typography was Engineering Accepted in earlier rounds but the O5F package showed no local labels; this round replaces that gap with a live four-viewport loaded-face proof at the current head.
